That's too bad. The main problem is that posts aren't often reported, and those that are (usually comments) don't break any of the community's rules. /v/gaming's modteam often brings rules forward for regular community review, but people don't always participate.

The current content creator guidelines address self-promotion, but only if it's ongoing and without other participation in the /v/gaming community. It doesn't stop one-time offenders and I risk overstepping my bounds if I interpret it that way.

Personally I think the crux of the issue is that participation across Voat seems to be dwindling. Last time this happened we had a sudden influx of users, but this time default subs are growing content-sparse. I try to contribute as much as I can, both here and in Voat's smaller gaming subs, but out of respect for the /v/gaming community I try to hold myself to the same three-posts-per hour rules that Voat imposes on non-moderators.

Bottom line is that we need more contributors. The good news is that the posts we do get often have great discussion on them; we just need more posts.

Edit: one thing you could try if you're interested in more gaming content is to set up an RSS feed with Feedly or Inoreader, or follow a gaming news aggregator like TheGamersPost.com. That way you're getting all of the news in real time, and you can choose what interesting stuff to post to /v/gaming. Inoreader has a customizable share button that lets you share directly to Voat's "submit link" page. And if you get in the habit of posting archive links, I have a bookmarklet over at /v/Efficiency that can automate that for you with a few easy clicks: https://voat.co/v/Efficiency/comments/968626

It's a different experience to be on the gathering and posting side of the fence, and it means the discussion comes straight to your inbox.
